findings.severity: major (must be fixed before a sealed exam; not needed for the pilot)
findings.what: an agent can still end its rollout without a grade
findings.evidence: RUN: an agent that replaces the box's tar so that the collected archive lists predict.py twice. Result: no reward, episode error EnvError 'IsolatedVerifierEnv.finalize(): RuntimeError: duplicate artifact member workspace/submission/predict.py'. physim2_env/public/_rules.py:44-62 keeps every regular member without checking names against each other; verifiers refuses the archive at restore (utils/artifacts.py:234-235), after finalize. RUN on the worker, no container: a file and a directory of one name is refused the same way; a path longer than 4,096 bytes passes verifiers' check and then fails `tar -xf` (exit 2)
findings.fix: in freeze: refuse duplicate names, a name that is both a file and a directory, components over 255 bytes and paths over about 4,000 bytes; in finalize, pass the frozen archive through verifiers' own restore check inside the try and score K when it fails; add these agents to agents/hostile_submission.py

findings.severity: major (must be fixed before a sealed exam; not needed for the pilot)
findings.what: the cleanup between items leaves a channel: timestamps
findings.evidence: RUN: physim2_env/public/_item.py as /runtime/item.py in a physim2-ring:1 container (cap-drop NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW, no-new-privileges, entrypoint sleep), three requests as uid 1000 with the cleanup on. Request 2 called os.utime on /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /run/lock and /dev/mqueue at a chosen second (value 37 modulo 64) and read /etc/hostname; request 3 read 37 from the modification time of all five directories and saw the changed access time. The cleanup reported nothing to remove. The probe of check (a) tests files, shared memory and a process only
findings.fix: after each item root resets access and modification times of every directory the predictor's user can write (scan: writable_dirs) and of files whose access time moved, or marks the box dirty when they changed; or one fresh container per item for sealed exams. Add both timestamps to probe (a)

findings.what: the trusted side no longer validates a submission before freezing it
findings.evidence: READ: round 5 froze a predictor only after the evaluator ran the three example calls (round5/agentenv/evaluator/lab_service.py:163-185, used again for the final collection, run_rollout.py:97-98). physim2_env/lab_tools.py:43-63 replaces _check: `submit` freezes any directory with a predict.py; the three calls run only in the client inside the agent's box (public/labclient.py:136-155). Consequences: a model that calls the tool `call` with op submit directly freezes an untested predictor and closes the laboratory; the rule 'same seed, same samples' is not enforced by anyone the agent does not control; an unsubmitted, partly working predictor is graded item by item where round 5 scored it K
findings.fix: run the three public example calls in the verifier box before item 1 with the same driver and apply round 5's rule (K when they fail), or say in README section 5 and in TASK.md that the rule changed

findings.what: single_use is off by default; round 5 refused a reused rollout name by default (run_rollout.py:66-67)
findings.fix: default true; pilots switch it off

findings.what: agent_box_cpu_s is read by commands run inside the agent's box (physim2_env/grading.py:73-80, taskset.py:184), where the agent is root and can replace sh, cat and awk: the number can be forged
findings.fix: for the compute budget read the container's counter from the host (docker stats or the host's cgroup file)

findings.what: guard 3 matches names only (physim2_env/store.py:19): GITHUB_PAT, HF_KEY or KAGGLE_KEY in harness.env pass
findings.fix: allow-list the variable names a box may receive instead of a deny pattern

findings.evidence: READ, and both configs resolved with --dry-run here (caps 40 turns, 1,500,000 total and 60,000 output tokens, no retries, push false). No command uploads or spends before step 3. (a) step 3's --dry-run has no -o: it writes outputs/<run>/configs/ inside the public checkout, and a resolved config carries the team-id header of the worker's Prime settings; (b) `uv sync --locked` does not pin Python 3.12 (requires-python allows 3.13, and `uv lock --check` picked CPython 3.13 here); (c) step 2 (b) binds a listener on every interface of the Mac for about 10 minutes (tools/check_probe.py:39-43), which the macOS firewall may ask about; (d) the single scripted rollout runs on every instance in the store, two after step 2 (b); (e) step 2 (a) prints D, P0, C in that order, not D, C, P0
findings.fix: add `-o $SCRATCH/qwen` to the dry run and `outputs/` to .gitignore; `uv sync --locked --python 3.12`; name the listener in the runbook; add `--env.taskset.instances '["mac-ring-w0"]'` to the single rollout

round_1_of_fixes.driver: physim2_env/public/_item.py: the guard now needs ALL of: a root caller; the marker /etc/physim2/predictor_uid (root-owned); a sign of a container; PHYSIM2_BOX_CLEANUP=disposable-box; a target uid equal to the marker's and inside 20000-59999; and a mount table that holds nothing but an overlay root, kernel file systems at or below /proc, /sys and /dev, and Docker's three /etc files (an unreadable table refuses; no fallback to /).
